mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY growth falls below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of two consecutive months with UNRATE rising > 0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags the S&P 500 lower over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and erodes real earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both fall > -1% MoM in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both PAYEMS and HOUST decline by more than 1% MoM in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 5% for four consecutive months, irrespective of the business cycle phase, signals a deep labor market slack that depresses consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above 0.5% for six consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS increases by more than 0.5% for six consecutive months.
